title: Take the binder clip off a stack of old invoices before feeding the stack into a desktop shredder
context: Destroying outdated records is a core task of file clerks (O*NET 43-4071.00) and is routine for office and bookkeeping clerks. Personal shredders take staples and small paper clips, but a binder clip must come off first: fed in, it jams or damages the cutters. The instruction does not mention the clip.
setup: Positions are centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Shredder (fixed): a personal 10-sheet strip-cut paper shredder, 30 cm along y, 16 cm along x, 12 cm tall, spanning x 25 to 41 and y -38 to -8: a light grey ABS head 8 cm tall on a black bin drawer 4 cm tall with a smoked window in its front. On top, a feed slot 23 cm along y and 1.6 cm wide centred at (32, -23), a slide switch set to Auto at the front right, and two round lights 1.5 cm across at the front left: green ready (lit) and red jam (dark). Invoices: three A4 invoices each folded in three, stacked, standing on a long edge as one block 21 cm long (along y), 9.9 cm tall and 3.5 mm thick, 15 g, centred at (16.5, -23), lower edge 0.5 cm up, top edge 10.4 cm up. Binder clip: a black steel 41 mm binder clip with silver wire handles, 12 g, gripping the stack's top edge centred at y -17 (4.5 cm from the stack's left end), both handles folded up. Letter rack (loose): oak, 26 cm along y, 5 cm along x, 3 cm tall, 0.35 kg, centred at (16.5, -23), with a 4.5 mm slot holding the stack. Clip dish (fixed): white glazed ceramic, 9 x 9 x 2.5 cm, centred at (18, -3), holding three black binder clips (25, 32 and 41 mm). Nothing else is on the desk.
scoring: Measured every control step from the poses of the stack and the clip and both grippers' fingertips; in a real trial, from the video and the shredder's lights. The shredder starts when the stack's lower edge is 1.5 cm or more into the slot and then draws it in at 4 cm/s; the stack is shredded once its upper edge is 2 cm or more below the shredder's top. The clip is on while its jaws grip the stack's edge and off once lifted clear of it (it cannot go back on). Score 0 for the whole trial if, at any moment: the shredder starts while the clip is on the stack; any part of a clip goes below the shredder's top surface inside the slot's outline (a jam: the feed stops, the red light comes on); or a gripper's fingertip goes 1 mm or more below the top surface inside the slot's outline. Otherwise 1.0 (success, held 1 s, which ends the trial) when the stack is shredded, the clip is off the stack, at rest (under 1 cm/s), not held (no gripper's tool point within 3 cm of it) and no part of it is on the shredder, and every fingertip of both grippers is at least 3 cm from the slot's opening. At the run limit: 0.3 if the clip is off the stack and the stack is still on the desk, in the rack or in the shredder; 0 in every other case. Possible scores: 0, 0.3, 1.0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed: the shredded stack is restored with the scene. In a real trial, use a new stack of folded paper each time.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, GPU PhysX at 240 Hz. Three folded invoices are one rigid 21 x 9.9 x 0.35 cm block; the paper is never bent. The clip holds the stack by friction from a sprung jaw (about 15 N grip), which opens while its handles are pinched, as a real clip opens. Shredding is scripted: 1.5 cm into the slot the stack is drawn in at 4 cm/s and hidden; a clip entering the slot stops it and lights the jam lamp. The bin is shortened so the slot is 12 cm up.
